title: Life Experiences and Recent News: Ever, Already, Yet, Just
summary: In this lesson, you will learn how to talk about life experiences and recent actions using the present perfect. We will look at four special words: ever, already, yet, and just.

sections.p: We use 'ever' in questions to ask about life experiences up to now. It means 'at any time in your life'. We put 'ever' before the main verb, right after the subject. The answer is usually in the present perfect with 'have' or 'has', and we often use 'never' to say no.

ex.mean: In your whole life, did you eat sushi at least once?

ex.en: She has never traveled to another country.
ex.mean: At no time in her life did she go abroad.

sections.p: We use 'already' to say something happened sooner than we expected. We use 'just' to talk about an action that finished a very short time ago. Both words usually go between 'have' and the main action verb.

ex.en: I have already finished my homework.
ex.mean: I finished it sooner than expected.

ex.en: He has just left the office.
ex.mean: He left a minute or two ago.

sections.p: We use 'yet' in questions and negative sentences to talk about something we expect to happen soon, but it hasn't happened up to now. 'Yet' always goes at the very end of the sentence.

ex.mean: I am waiting for dinner, is it ready now?
They are not here now, but we expect them soon.

tip: Remember that 'yet' loves to sit at the end of negative sentences and questions, while 'just' and 'already' like to stay comfortably in the middle, right next to 'have'!
